Subject: MAP kickoff: success tests, exit probes, and candidate smoke window

Hi Amelia —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, I put together an initial Mutual Action Playbook (attached) that focuses on the evaluation success criteria we agreed on: latency & throughput thresholds, hallucination/concordance checks on the clinical summaries, and security evidence for the SOC2 items you requested.

High-level ask: please review the attached sheet and confirm the owners & realistic windows for each item. Key pieces we want to lock this week so the evaluation sprint can run the week of Oct 5: 

- Acceptance tests (automated + manual) for 3 sample workflows (patient intake, summary generation, triage flagging)
- Exit probes (what constitutes a fail vs. acceptable degradation)
- Final smoke window for canary cutover and production-like load validation (we're proposing Oct 7 10:00–13:00 PDT)

I've included a compact checklist (criteria-bakeoff-checklist.pdf) that maps each criterion to pass/fail thresholds. If that window works for you, we can schedule the engineering runbook review with Mina this Friday.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm owners on the sheet by EOD Wednesday
2) We finalize the SOW tie-outs (attached SOW draft)
3) Marissa and Mina run the test harness and share the smoke-run commands for your infra team

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the spreadsheet.

Jonas
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CRH_MAP_v1.xlsx (workbook), criteria-bakeoff-checklist.pdf (one-pager), SOW-draft_20260928.pdf (draft)

Jonas —

Thanks for the package. Quick notes after a first pass:

- Owners: I'll own clinical validation (with Rajiv supporting on data prep).
- Window: Oct 7 10:00–13:00 PDT is OK but can we shrink the smoke window to 90 minutes if the first pass hits all top-line tests? We have limited weekday ops coverage.
- Criteria: For hallucination tolerance, we need a clear definition — the checklist currently references a 95% concordance figure but doesn't specify test prompt sets. Can you add the exact prompts and sample expected outputs?

Also, two security asks before we run anything: a short summary of PKI requirements (hardware vs. software keys) and confirmation that token logs will be available for the smoke window.

I'll get back with owners/ETA on Wed.

Best,
Amelia

Amelia —

Thanks for the quick reply. Short answers inline: 

- Prompt sets: I've uploaded a compact zip of three prompt suites to the shared doc link (see related_links). Each suite targets one of the evaluation workflows. I'll paste the clinical-summary prompt below for transparency.

- Concordance: the bakeoff checklist uses a combination metric: precision on key entities (drug, dose, condition) >= 97% plus a human-rated coherence score >= 4/5 on a 50-sample holdout. If either metric fails, the run is considered a non-pass and triggers the exit probes.

- Smoke window: Oct 7 10:00–11:30 PDT accepted (90 minutes) — we'll plan for an early hard-fail cutoff at 11:00 if we see any critical errors to avoid downstream load on your systems.

- PKI/token logs: Redwood supports both software-backed keys and HSM/KMS integrations. For the smoke run, we will provide token-level session logs and a short doc on key management options.

I'll coordinate with Marissa to draft the runbook and the specific run commands. Can we do a 30-min engineer-to-engineer call Friday 09/26 at 10:00 PDT to finalize the harness?

Cheers,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Platform Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Mina / Jonas —

Thanks — Friday's 10:00 call worked well. Quick note to confirm next steps and the acceptance tests we signed off on: 

1) Clinical prompt set (50 holdout) — pass requires entity precision >= 97% AND coherence >= 4/5 (manual).
2) Latency under load — 95th percentile token latency < 180ms at a sustained 10 rps for 90 seconds.
3) Throughput/kv-cache sanity — successful KV cache warmup within 3 minutes, and no more than 5% token error rate during the window.
4) Security gating — token logs and session audit exported to our S3 location; confirmation of KMS policy alignment from your security contacts.

Assignees:
- Clinical validation: Amelia / Rajiv
- Load validation & runbook: Mina / Marissa
- Procurement/SOW: Rajiv / Jonas (we'll start the SOW review Monday)

If all of the above pass in the Oct 7 10:00–11:30 PDT window, Cedar Ridge will sign the final SOW with the initial reserved capacity commit listed in the draft. If any critical exit probe trips, we'll pause and reconvene on mitigation and a re-run date.

I'll also upload a short internal checklist for the ops folks — will share the link to that doc within the hour.

Appreciate the team moving quickly.

Amelia
Head of Clinical Ops
Cedar Ridge Health
